cells.tense: You are choosing your direction now, and the fairness in it is plain to you.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Let something already finished end — close it, honor what it was, don't reopen it. Leave the ground it clears empty for a couple of days.
cells.core:
You can point yourself where you mean to go, and the fairness in it flows without effort. You don't keep a ledger — you simply know what belongs where, and it moves both directions, giving and receiving in the same breath. When something tips off true you feel it and set it right without turning it into a case.

Part of what you're carrying is already finished. Let it end on purpose: close it, honor what it was, and don't reopen it. The space it leaves doesn't need to be filled right away. Some of the weight belongs on other people's side of the line, and it can stay there — it isn't yours to collect. What's over doesn't need your hand to stay over.
cells.sheetLine: You can say what's owed without keeping score.
cells.verb: Recalibrating what's out of proportion until balance returns

cells.tense: You are bracing toward what will be asked of you before anyone has asked.
cells.act: carry it without tightening around it
cells.ask: Take one demand on your direction and hold it with nothing else running — no renegotiating, no deciding, no counting who did what. Then put it down.
cells.core:
On the way to what you've chosen, a ledger runs. Who gave what, who hasn't matched it, what you're owed before the next step is allowed. The fairness you naturally have is doing overtime, and it's started to slow the very thing it was guarding. Anyone moving with you can feel the scale in their hands.

Hold the next piece without tightening around it. Choose the demand you'll carry, keep your shape under it, and stop tallying for that stretch. The goal is the only thing you track. If a piece ends up carried by nobody, you'll spot it plainly at the end and can settle it once, cleanly, rather than at every step of the way.
cells.sheetLine: The accounting is slowing what you're choosing.
cells.verb: Recalibrating what's out of proportion until balance returns
cells.place: where you choose direction and say 'this, not that'

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Do the plain practice today, alone, the version you know by heart — even if it feels like nothing. Keep the session steady, and when it ends, stay a moment and let what you put out this week be seen at its true size.
cells.core:
Here, fairness runs one way — outward. You choose a direction and give what you give, and what should come back arrives elsewhere, or doesn't arrive. Standing in a direction has come to mean standing without asking. The door is behind you and your body hasn't moved.

Do the plain practice today, kept lit by attention rather than by any flash of result. When it's done, stay a moment and let what you put out be seen at its true size — no asking yet, no fixing, no argument with anyone. The practice itself is the act, and whatever it shows you can wait until tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You stand, but you don't claim what standing asks.
cells.verb: Recalibrating what's out of proportion until balance returns
cells.place: where you choose direction and say 'this, not that'

cells.tense: You are writing a ledger in a room where you believe the pen is down.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Next time something feels off with someone, wait before you weigh it. Notice what you already knew before the reasons arrived — the first thing that landed — and start from there. Leave the rest alone.
cells.core:
Something in you is keeping score without telling you. Balances are monitored, what's owed is tracked, and you'd say you weren't doing it — you're just going along. You are directing your attention somewhere, and a quiet part is writing in the margins about what should come back to you.

What's true is simpler than the running count. Next time you notice the tilt, wait for the first thing that lands, before the reasons arrive, and begin with that instead. What you already knew about it is more accurate than the tally. The numbers can rest; you didn't know you were keeping them anyway. One clear perception is enough to work from.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping a score you don't know you're keeping.

attempts.check: The status's language of 'tolerance of unfair treatment' risks sliding into a claim about motives or history—I say only what fairness has to do with standing and choice now. A reader could object that no one ever asked them to claim anything, or that this seat is already theirs. The ask survives being wrong: looking back at one exchange and naming what was fair can be done whether they were taken from or simply not in the habit of asking. The sentence serving me more than them is the one that locates this in their body as 'resonance' or in their past as a cause—I keep it on the present act of naming the balance and standing when it's off.
